newsitem.title: USA: US late spot prods mixed in thin holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: US late spot prods mixed in thin holiday trade.

text.p: U.S. spot oil products prices were mixed in ultra-thin Veteran's Day trade Monday, players said, with Gulf Coast conventional unleaded gasoline jumping sharply on continued keen interest and tight supply, players said.

Gulf Coast traders said differentials firmed about two cents a gallon for "M4" conventional unleaded, with material sold for 3.75 cents over December futures and offers rising to five cents over by late afternoon.
"It's scheduling day on the 32nd cycle and a couple of buyers stepped up," one Gulf trader said, noting that the gains were partly offset by a 0.25 cent declne in NYMEX December futures.

Differentials on New York Harbor conventional "M5" unleaded were steady at about 3.25 cents over the print, with traders citing spotty action amid the U.S. national holiday and an industry event in Washington, D.C.
Heating oil diffs, meanwhile, fell about 0.60 cent tracking NYMEX and stable differentials.
Gulf and NYH cash prices and the NYMEX screen were little affected by news of a morning fire at Texaco's 98,000 barrel per day refinery in the Los Angeles suburb of Wilmington.
